subject.title: Safeguard compaction doesn't trigger during fast tool loops — 172K context paid per turn

question: Should OpenClaw compact proactively for tool-loop cost or density while the prompt still fits the model budget, and if so should that extend `midTurnPrecheck` or remain outside core policy?
rationale: The current implementation intentionally guards prompt-fit pressure; choosing a cost threshold, a no-progress definition, default behavior, and provider-independent accounting would create durable runtime and configuration policy.

options.title: Validate and extend the existing guard
options.body: Reproduce the reported loop, then add the smallest well-defined proactive trigger to `midTurnPrecheck` with upgrade-safe defaults and focused regression coverage.

options.title: Keep overflow-only semantics
options.body: Retain the existing opt-in guard as a context-fit recovery mechanism and document it as unsuitable for optimizing metered-but-still-fitting prompts.

options.title: Move cost policy out of core
options.body: Keep core focused on context safety and support an optional plugin or operational policy for provider-specific spend controls.

recommendation.title: Validate and extend the existing guard
recommendation.body: Reproduce the reported loop, then add the smallest well-defined proactive trigger to `midTurnPrecheck` with upgrade-safe defaults and focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing precheck whose boundary must be extended or explicitly retained.
